parts:
Hi 
I've been working on a project using Lavaan. It's a CFA model and I'm kind of new to CFA (and to lavaan, but the tutorial has been very helpful!). Everything is looking good except for one thing. My model is a longitudinal metric invariance in a 2-time, 3-indicator CFA (one factor with 3 indicators, repeated once). In particular, I'd like to know how to specify that the latent variance at time 2 is freely estimated. By default it's restricted to be 1. Also my variables are all categorical. I did try to look through the discussion board but didn't find anything specific to this. 
I'm writing the current model like this:
model<- 'time1 =~ FTOMFBRW + FTOMKARW +FTOMSPRW
                  time2 =~ STOMFBRW + STOMKARW+ STOMSPRW'
I've figured out how to make everything else freely estimate except for time 2

Thank you for your help,
 
Marcia L. Walsh-Aziz MS CCC-SLP
Speech, Language, and Hearing Department
Doctoral Student 
University of Colorado Boulder
815-954-4407

messages.subject: Re:
parts:
Are you using std.lv = TRUE?

Don't put that.  You need to identify the variance of the latent in some way - you need to identify the variance of the latent in some way - the best way (usually) is to constrain the first loading to be equal to 1 (which is what lavaan does, by default).

There's a paper about that sort of thing here: http://psycnet.apa.org/record/2002-13431-004

messages.author: b430763ad49e6cd0
messages.subject: Re:
parts: Thank you for your quick response. We initially ran it without using that code and it didn't do what we're trying to do. How do you specify std.lv=TRUE by naming the parameters?

If you want to use the fixed factor method ( standardised latent variances and means if you use them) to identify your model, and want to do so manually: 

To specify all latent variances to be 1 (part of the syntax): 

time1 ~~ V*time1
time2 ~~ V*time2

V == 1

Note that 'V' is just an example, you can give it whatever letter / name you want (e.g. VAR). 
If you are using means in your model, then you'd additionally specify:

time1 ~ M*1
time2 ~ M*1 

M == 0 

In lavaan "time1 ~ 1" specifies an intercept, you use the M so you can constrain it to 0. Since you're doing a longitudinal study, you're probably interested in the latent means. 

To specify only 1 latent variance to be 1: 

time1 ~~ V*time1
time2 ~~ time2

V == 1

The same idea for the latent means: 
time1 ~ M*1
time2 ~ 1

M == 0 

Note that you can also do it the other way around (i.e. specify time 2's variance to be 1 and time 1 to be freely estimated).

messages.subject: Re:
parts:
What are you trying to do?

Post code and (if possible) a reproducible example. You can specify std.lv = TRUE, but it's sometimes not a good idea (and when you're looking at invariance is one of those times).*

J

* A bit like analyzing a correlation matrix. Sometimes it matters, sometimes it doesn't. You can worry about whether it matters, and try to work it out, or you can just not do it. It's easier to not do it. (IMHO).
